Subject: Celestis - ephemeral log retention mapping and evidence request

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Celestis' security team is working through our SIG/CAIQ and we hit a few questions around Redwood's ephemeral logging (session traces, runtime-level debug captures, and KV cache access logs). Specifically: 

1) We need a mapping of each log class (runtime_traces, request_headers, kvcache_ops, audit_events) to the canonical retention TTL that Redwood applies in hosted deployments. Our compliance baseline is 30/90/365-day buckets and we require explicit justification for anything kept longer.

2) Evidence: a small redacted log sample (no PII, no customer prompt content) for each class, plus the retention enforcement mechanism (S3 lifecycle rule / DB TTL / job name) and timestamps showing deletion scheduling. For SOC 2/SIG we typically accept a redacted sample + policy text + a deletion job output showing a deleted key ID.

3) Customer-specific exceptions: we are evaluating a need for a 180-day exception on runtime_traces for our debugging SLA. Please include the exception approval workflow and any guardrails (who can approve, what legal review is required, audit trail) — and whether Redwood supports scoped exceptions per tenant.

Can you provide the artifacts or point me to a shared folder with the artifacts? Happy to sign an NDA or additional redaction attestation if needed.

Thanks,
Michael
Celestis Security

--

Quick draft of artifacts we can supply: 

- retention mapping (attached as redwood_log_retention_mapping.csv) — maps component -> default TTL -> mechanism -> enforcement owner. Example rows: runtime_traces, 90d, S3 lifecycle rule (prefix runtime_traces/), infra-retention-job-01.
- s3-lifecycle-policy.txt — canonical policy text used for hosted buckets (we can scope policies by bucket prefix to isolate tenants in Dedicated/Private).
- celestis_redacted_log_sample.json — one JSON object per class with all sensitive fields redacted and a truncated request id.
- deletion evidence: we can provide a job run log that shows a deleted object key and timestamp (we will redact object ids to a short hash).

Notes on exceptions: 
- Hosted: we support tenant-scoped retention overrides via a per-tenant metadata tag and a change control process. Approver chain: Security Manager -> Legal -> VP Product. All approvals create a ticket (Jira) and are recorded in the audit log.
- Dedicated/Private: tenant admins can request changes; for on-prem we provide deployment scripts and a signed addendum.

Limitations & mitigations: 
- We do not store customer prompt content in runtime_traces by default; prompts are redacted at the ingress layer for customers who opt-in for redaction. If Celestis requires full prompts for debugging we require an explicit change in contract (and an updated DPA).
- Forensics/legal hold: we support preserve-on-hold for specific object keys; we keep an immutable hold flag and a retention override until the release date. We can provide an exhibit of the audit trail for hold/unhold actions.

I will produce the CSV, sample JSON and S3 policy and upload to the Drive link by Thu 03/05. Neha pls confirm final approver chain wording.

- Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Michael — thanks for the patience. Attaching a short evidence bundle and summary below (also uploaded to the shared Drive). If you need additional redaction attestations we can produce those.

Summary: attached are three artifacts: redwood_log_retention_mapping.csv (mapping of log classes to TTL/mechanism), celestis_redacted_log_sample.json (one redacted sample per class), and s3-lifecycle-policy.txt (hosted S3 lifecycle rule snippet used for automatic expiration). We have also included a short text excerpt showing a deletion job run that removed a sample object; the object id is obfuscated to a short hash.

Key points: 
- Default retention for runtime_traces in hosted deployments: 90 days.
- KV cache operation logs and short-lived debug traces: 30 days.
- Audit_events (security/audit) and billing traces: 365 days.
- We support tenant-scoped exceptions in Hosted via metadata-tagged prefixes; approval flow: Security Manager -> Legal -> VP Product. The request is captured in Jira and the approval is appended to the tenant metadata change.

Regarding Celestis' ask for 180 days on runtime_traces: we can support a scoped exception in Hosted, subject to a documented business justification and Legal sign-off. Controls we would require: encrypted-at-rest (KMS key either customer-managed or Redwood-managed with access attestation), scoped access logs to list who read the traces, and a rolling review every 90 days. We estimate a one-time security review and a small surcharge to cover extended storage costs.

Next steps: 
- If Celestis wants to pursue the 180-day exception, please send a short justification (1–2 paragraphs) and indicate whether you require customer-managed KMS. I will start a Jira request and route it to Legal.
- If you want additional evidence for SOC 2, we can provide a sanitized deletion job run showing the job id and timestamp (same hash redaction approach).

Files attached: redwood_log_retention_mapping.csv; celestis_redacted_log_sample.json; s3-lifecycle-policy.txt

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
